source: ACIAR AH/2005/086 'Smallholder Cattle Best Practice Manual' (Windsor, Bush & Young), Best Practice Health and Husbandry of Cattle, Cambodia -- hosted at mekonglivestock.wordpress.com (University of Sydney / GDAHP project site)
text: The manual recommends body condition scoring (BCS) as a simple, practical way to evaluate an animal's productive state, by rating appearance or (better) by palpation on a 1 (very skinny) to 5 (very fat) scale, checking the ribs, brisket, backline, and hip prominence -- healthy animals should show a covering of flesh over bony points. Breeding animals should be at least BCS 2, ideally 2.5-3; animals below BCS 1.5 are in poor health and need investigation, either from inadequate feed (e.g. a lactating cow not getting enough quality forage) or from an underlying disease. The manual notes that unfortunately many cattle in Cambodia sit at BCS 1.5 or below.
